newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds fell on continued concerns about the Swiss franc, which pushed prices down sharply in the shorter maturities.
"It was a debacle. The short end especially was under pressure because the weak franc is pushing down prices. There was dramatic selling," one Swiss head bond trader said.
He said the downward pressure on prices could intensify if the Swiss franc, now teetering on the brink of key levels against the dollar and mark, falls further.
The dollar traded around 1.27 Swiss francs, and the mark to just shy of 84.00 centimes late on Monday.
The December confederate bond futures contract set a one-month low, dipping back to 114.11 which took out the previous low of 114.15 touched twice in October.

Argentina launched a seven-year 200 million Swiss franc foreign bond with a coupon of 7.00 percent, which was priced at 102.25. The issue was quoted in afternoon trade at 7.00 percent midpoint, between bid and offer. The offer was led by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Banque Paribas.
One trader said demand for the deal was "normal" with respect to the high coupon. He said that the issue was aimed at retail investors rather than institutionals.
For that reason, traders expected demand to be slow at the outset but expected it to pick up in two or three weeks.
Dec Conf futures down six at 114.25.
Dec Comi medium-term bond off 15 at 109.90
Mar Euro Swiss francs down 18 at 97.59.
